title: Transformers & LLM Applications
why: Transformers power modern language, vision and code models; knowing the mechanism makes you better at using and evaluating them.
explain: A transformer processes a sequence of token embeddings with self-attention. Each token forms a query, a key and a value vector. Attention weights = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) say how much each token reads from every other token, and the output is the weighted sum of the values. Multiple heads attend to different relationships in parallel.

A block is attention plus a feed-forward network, each wrapped in a residual connection and layer normalization. Positional information is added because attention alone does not know order. A language model applies a causal mask so token t sees only tokens up to t, and trains by predicting the next token with cross-entropy.

Large language models are these networks scaled up, then adapted with prompting, retrieval (RAG), fine-tuning (including parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA) and tool use. Evaluating an LLM feature means building task-specific test sets, checking faithfulness to the sources and tracking cost and latency, not trusting demos.
key_points: Causal masking makes next-token training possible
Residual connections and layer norm keep deep stacks trainable
RAG for fresh or private knowledge; fine-tuning for style and behavior
Evaluate LLM features on your own test set, with regression checks
pitfalls: Forgetting the causal mask lets the model peek at the answer during training
Evaluating generation quality on a few cherry-picked prompts

leetcode.why: A monotonic deque handles windowed maxima, the pattern behind local and sliding-window attention.
Finding the smallest window that satisfies a condition mirrors selecting minimal context.
An LRU cache is the intuition behind key-value caching during generation.
Stack-based decoding of nested structure builds the habit needed for parsing and tokenization logic.
Longest common subsequence underlies text-similarity metrics such as ROUGE-L.

industry.q: Why are attention scores divided by the square root of the key dimension?
key_points: Dot products grow with dimension, pushing softmax into saturation
Saturated softmax gives tiny gradients and unstable training

key_points: Knowledge that changes often points to RAG
Fine-tune for tone, format or specialized behavior
Compare cost, latency, evaluation, citation needs and privacy

industry.q: How do you evaluate an LLM-powered feature before launch?
key_points: A representative labeled test set and a clear rubric
Automatic checks plus human review; spot-check any LLM-as-judge
A regression suite rerun on every prompt or model change
